title: I Used the Drum-Sander Paper Log on the Intern Who Hijacked My Grit

parts.text: I stepped into sander bay at 3:06 p.m. and intern Cleo was already using my numbered grit. The board said: THIRTY MINUTES. GRIT STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-nine, finish lead, holding a clipboard that listed our pass. Cleo shrugged. "Interns share the drum." I photographed the board, the booking, and her stock on my paper. Then I asked for the paper log. At 3:14 the finish desk pinged why Cleo's stock sat on our paper. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The finish desk can see Cleo's stock on the drum during our pass.

social.video_title: She hijacked my numbered sander grit — Part 1/2
social.description: Drum sander, an intern on my paper, a thirty-minute clock she posted. I logged the stock. Would you have asked for the paper log?

parts.text: Cleo called it test passes until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the drum still. The grit went back to my numbered sleeve. Cleo ran a slot of their own and told the next intern atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: INTERNS DO NOT SHARE A BOOKED DRUM. I keep our pass on a labeled card. Cleo brown-bags her stock. The sander finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Interns do not share a booked drum — Part 2/2
social.description: Paper log, numbered grit, and a second line on the board. Were test passes ever our grit?
